title: The Little Free War
description: Two neighbors on Maple Court each built a Little Free Library, eleven feet apart, and now run them like rival nations with bylaws, stamps, and a blacklist. Ronnie booked it to celebrate literacy. It does not stay literacy.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and tonight we celebrate something beautiful. Two neighbors on Maple Court, each with their own little free library, sharing books with the whole block. Patricia, Winston, welcome.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: They're eleven feet apart, Ronnie. That's not a community. That's a border.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Eleven feet of pure literacy, Barry. That's just good neighboring. Patricia, tell us about your little box.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Thank you, Ronnie. My little box is open to everyone. Everyone who follows the rules. We have a sign-out sheet, a return window of fourteen days, and a stamp for every patron in good standing.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Rules. She has a stamp. <p:0.3> Ronnie, Box Two does not need a stamp, because Box Two is curated.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Curated. He put four cookbooks and a phone directory in a wooden box, sweetheart.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Curated, Patricia. CURATED.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Patricia, what happens if someone keeps a book past fourteen days?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Then they go on the list, Barry.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: ...The list.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: The no-return blacklist. Their name goes on the laminated card taped inside the door, and my little box will not open for them again.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Patricia, that's a community freezeout. That's racketeering with paperbacks.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now that's just standards, Barry. A box has to have standards.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: She blacklisted a nine-year-old, Ronnie. The Hadley boy. He kept a Goosebumps for sixteen days.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: He knew the window, Winston. Everyone knows the window. <p:0.3> And you took my regulars, so do not lecture me about children.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I did not take them. They migrated. To a curated collection.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, hi! Longtime listener. I just wanted the next book in the Inspector Pemberton series, and neither box has it anymore?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: That's because someone is EMPTYING us, Linda.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, that sounds lovely! I mean, no, that sounds awful.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Yeah, hi. <p:0.3> Longtime listener. Real quick. About the, uh, the emptying.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: ...Who is this?

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Nobody. A neighbor. So allegedly, a person might take everything out of both boxes around five a.m. <p:0.3> And allegedly sell it at the flea market by nine. Allegedly.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: You're the FENCE? You've been selling my curated ecosystem at a FOLDING TABLE?

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: I move volume. Allegedly. A dollar a hardcover. The Pemberton ones go for two.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh! So if I come to your table, I could finally get book four?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Linda, no, he stole it from the box you already have access to.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Booth twelve. Allegedly. Bring small bills.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, that's redistribution, Barry. The books are reaching new readers. That's just good neighboring.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, that's grand theft and operating an unlicensed resale operation.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: I want him on the list. Phil. P-H-I-L. He goes on the laminated card tonight.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Fine. Blacklist him from YOUR box. He's already barred from Box Two, because Box Two is CURATED.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Funny thing about Box Two, Winston. <p:0.3> I empty it every morning. So how come there's always cash taped under the bottom shelf?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: ...Cash. Under the shelf.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Rolls of it. Rubber-banded. Behind a phone directory nobody's ever checked out.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: That is... that is a curated reserve, Phil.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: A curated RESERVE. <p:0.3> Winston, you're not running a library, you're running a wash. The books are just the receipts.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, Box Two is laundering money. The little free library is a front.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: It is a CURATED front, Barry!

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Blacklist!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Curated!

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: Booth twelve!

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Book four!

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: You laundered my readers, Winston!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I CURATED them, Patricia!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, they're yelling about a money-laundering box eleven feet from a fence.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And isn't that something, Barry. <p:0.3> A blacklist, a flea-market fence, and cash under the shelf. Folks, that is the most literate block in the city.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, between all that, the only thing anyone's actually read is a cooked ledger.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: So... does anybody have book four?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: The box will see you tonight, Phil.

lines.speaker: caller-phil
lines.text: ...That's not, that's not a library thing to say.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That's just good neighboring. We'll be right back, soon as somebody returns that shelf cash. Fourteen-day window.
